transcript.text:
A washer will usually refuse to spin until it has drained, so retained water is the first thing to separate. The other common possibility is an unbalanced load — especially one bulky item, a bath mat, duvet or a very small load — which is often normal behaviour rather than a fault. 1. When it reaches spin, look through the door: is there water still in the drum? If yes, this points to a drain blockage, hose restriction or pump problem rather than the spin motor.
2. Listen near the bottom while it tries to drain. A hum with no water leaving usually means a blockage in the filter/pump path or drain hose; complete silence can be the pump or its control circuit.
3. If the drum is empty, try a spin with a normal mixed, evenly spread load — not a single heavy item. If it then spins, it was an imbalance issue. When checking anything by hand, switch off and unplug the machine first. If water is left inside, do not open the pump filter until you have towels or a shallow tray ready, as water can come out quickly.
no water left in the drum, its empty. it was just a big heavy bath mat on its own, came out dripping. no error code. drum sloshes about and tries to speed up then slows down a few times

This sounds most like normal imbalance protection, not a failed spin motor. A single heavy, water-soaked bath mat sticks to one side of the drum; the machine then rocks the load around and repeatedly attempts to speed up, but abandons the spin to avoid excessive banging. It will leave the mat dripping wet. 1. Take the bath mat out and run a spin with a normal mixed, evenly spread load of ordinary laundry. If it spins properly, there is no fault.
2. For future mat washes, avoid spinning one on its own. Wash it with a few suitable items to balance it, provided the mat’s care label allows machine washing and spinning.
3. If it also repeatedly aborts with ordinary balanced loads, especially if the machine bangs, moves about or is unstable, then check it is firm and level on the floor. Persistent failure with balanced loads would point more towards suspension or levelling and may need an engineer. No error code and an empty drum both fit the imbalance explanation here.
ok i tried the mat with a couple of towels, rinse and spin and it spun fine, mat came out damp not dripping. so its fine then?

Yes — it sounds fine. The machine was correctly detecting that the bath mat on its own was too unbalanced to spin safely. It completed the spin and the mat came out normally damp rather than dripping, which shows the drive and spin function are working. For mats, duvets and other heavy absorbent items, avoid spinning them alone; add a few suitable towels or similar items to help distribute the load, provided the care labels allow it. If it ever refuses to spin a normal mixed load as well, that would be worth investigating — but there is no sign of a fault from this test.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that.
